summary: The server crashes when attempting to load chunks that contain command blocks that consist of large numbers of characters within the previous output field
description: The Bug: The server crashes when attempting to load chunks that contain command blocks that consist of large numbers of characters within the previous output field. The full server console log and a crash report regarding this have been attached and can be found below. Stack Trace: [^crash-2022-04-27_10.42.38-server.txt] Description: Exception generating new chunk java.io.EOFException at java.base/java.io.DataInputStream.readUnsignedShort(DataInputStream.java:346) at pq.a(SourceFile:54) at pq$1.a(SourceFile:34) at oz$1.a(SourceFile:136) at pu$b.a(SourceFile:50) at pf$1.a(SourceFile:91) at oz$1.a(SourceFile:96) at pj.a(SourceFile:120) at cvr.a(SourceFile:65) at cvo.b(SourceFile:218) at cvo.a(SourceFile:231) at awt$b.run(SourceFile:59) at awr.h(SourceFile:91) at awr.a(SourceFile:146) at awr.run(SourceFile:102) at java.base/java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor.runWorker(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:1136) at java.base/java.util.concurrent.ThreadPoolExecutor$Worker.run(ThreadPoolExecutor.java:635) at java.base/java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:833) Steps to Reproduce: - Launch a server running 22w16b that has command blocks enabled and join it. - Unlock all recipes within the game by executing the command provided below. /recipe give @s - Summon a repeating command block nearby that will constantly get the data of your player. /setblock ~ ~ ~3 minecraft:repeating_command_block{auto:1b,Command:"data get entity @p"} - Leave the game, shut down the server, and reboot it. - Take note as to whether or not the server crashes when attempting to load chunks that contain command blocks that consist of large numbers of characters within the previous output field. Observed Behavior: The server crashes. Expected Behavior: The server would not crash.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch a server running 22w16b with command blocks enabled and join it.  
2. Execute the command ``/recipe give @s`` to unlock all recipes.  
3. Execute the command ``/setblock ~ ~ ~3 minecraft:repeating_command_block{auto:1b,Command:"data get entity @p"}`` to place a repeating command block that constantly gets player data.  
4. Wait at least a few minutes so the command block’s previous output field grows to contain many characters.  
5. Disconnect from the server and shut it down.  
6. Restart the server.  
7. Observe whether the server crashes when loading the chunk that contains the command block.
Observed Behavior: When the server attempts to load a chunk that contains a command block whose previous‑output field stores a very large string, the server process terminates abruptly and a crash report is generated. The console log records an “Exception generating new chunk” followed by a java.io.EOFException thrown while reading an unsigned short from a DataInputStream, and the stack trace shows calls through the internal chunk‑loading classes (pq, oz, pu, pf, cvr, cvo) before reaching the thread‑pool executor and the Java thread run method. The crash occurs during server startup after the world has been saved with the oversized command‑block data; the server does not finish loading the affected chunk, the world may become locked and disappear from the server list, and no further gameplay can continue. This behavior deviates from the expected outcome, where the server should load the chunk successfully and continue running despite the large command‑block output.
Expected Behavior: When the server is restarted after the described steps, it should successfully generate and load the chunk containing the repeating command block, regardless of the length of the text stored in the command block’s previous output field. The command block should retain its data, the world should remain accessible, and no crash or exception should occur during chunk loading.
